principles: Detect-and-prompt over auto-fix: stale state must surface explicitly with copy-paste recovery, never silently refresh
Single source of truth: reuse checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit and DIRTY_WORKTREE_CATEGORIES rather than duplicate freshness/category logic
Same vocabulary across all surfaces: session_brief, story_advance pre-check, and koala validate must use identical EVIDENCE STALE marker and command format
drivers: B-c9f5 field report showed extended REVIEW/TEST loops when users had no actionable next step after main merge
B-6326 pitfalls note recorded the exact 3-step recovery incantation, proving the gap is UX not mechanism
Multiple surfaces currently diverge: hints.ts:203 prints stale advice in validate path only; session_brief and story_advance are silent

options.name: A: Surface stale state at every entry point + single-shot recover command
pros: Users see the same EVIDENCE STALE marker no matter which command they ran
recover_evidence reduces 3 manual steps to 1 explicit command
Refuse condition (non-koala_metadata dirt present) prevents masking real drift
Reuses existing checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit and classifier — no new logic for detection
cons: Touches 3 handlers (session.ts, story-advance.ts, validate hint surface) and adds 1 new CLI handler — more files than a one-spot fix

options.name: B: Only fix the koala validate output (hints.ts:203 already has it)
pros: Minimal diff; just normalize the existing hint to use EVIDENCE STALE marker
cons: Users who first run session_brief or story_advance still hit the silent failure case
Does not address the B-c9f5 pattern where users debug via session_brief first

options.name: C: Auto-recover on detect (silent refresh)
pros: Zero user action required after main merge
cons: Silently passes materially-regressed evidence — exactly the contamination the freshness check exists to prevent
Violates B-6326 conservative-policy principle: classification explains but does not loosen blocking
Hides the merge-cost from users so they cannot reason about why the gate is green

chosen: A: Surface stale state at every entry point + single-shot recover command
rationale: Choose A because the reported failure is purely UX gap, not a mechanism gap. Detection exists (checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit), recovery command exists (verification_evidence_refresh_stale). The fix is wiring the existing pieces into every surface where users land, plus a one-command convenience wrapper. Reject B because session_brief is the canonical entry point per CLAUDE.md 0 and silent failure there forces users back into the validate path for diagnosis. Reject C because it violates the conservative classification principle from B-6326 — auto-refresh would mask real materialHash drift caused by genuine source regressions.

preMortem.scenario: recover_evidence runs but masks a real material regression because classifier missed a category
preMortem.trigger: DIRTY_WORKTREE_CATEGORIES gets a new category added without updating recover_evidence refuse-condition list
preMortem.consequence: User runs recover_evidence after merging main with a real broken file; refresh succeeds, validate re-runs and passes against new hash, user advances to DONE with regressed code
preMortem.mitigation: recover_evidence refuse-list must use the SAME DIRTY_WORKTREE_CATEGORIES enum (whitelist koala_metadata + runtime + declared_artifact); any new category added defaults to refuse. Cover with smoke that asserts an unknown future category does NOT pass through.

preMortem.scenario: EVIDENCE STALE marker drifts between surfaces (session_brief uses STALE EVIDENCE, validate uses Evidence Stale)
preMortem.trigger: Implementer copies hint formatting from one surface to another without sharing a constant
preMortem.consequence: Users cannot grep/anchor on the marker; recovery automation breaks; B-c9f5 UX gap returns
preMortem.mitigation: Define a single exported constant EVIDENCE_STALE_MARKER and exported renderEvidenceStaleHint(storyId) function; all three surfaces call it. Smoke test asserts byte-identical output across surfaces.

preMortem.scenario: Copy-paste command uses placeholder instead of actual storyId after a refactor
preMortem.trigger: Implementer extracts the hint into a generic helper without piping storyId through
preMortem.consequence: Users have to know to substitute the placeholder; many will not; B-c9f5 incident repeats
preMortem.mitigation: renderEvidenceStaleHint(storyId) accepts storyId as required arg; smoke asserts output contains B-a2f1 literally and does not contain placeholder strings.
